body:
T139 left this behind, deliberately and visibly.

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. The test titled "the render clock is the OPERATOR'S clock: a 1ms budget times out
even the trivial renderer" no longer serves the trivial renderer. It serves the `hang` route, under
the authorization merged in #405. That swap was forced: a trivial bundle finishes inside 1ms often
enough that the assertion decided on scheduling, and the rail fired red on a windows runner after
passing on linux.

WHAT IS WRONG. The rail's COMMENT still argues from the trivial bundle -- "One millisecond against a
trivial bundle can only time out if the knob genuinely governs the worker." A hang stops under any
clock, so the assertion no longer carries that argument. The comment is frozen, so #405's one-line
pair could not reach it. This is the exact shape CLAUDE.md names: an honest-looking comment over a
weaker test.

NOTHING IS UNCOVERED. The property the comment claims is railed deterministically in
test/gateway/render-spawn-forwarding.test.ts -- the token door hands the worker
`gw.options.renderTimeoutMs`, and a site that stops doing so reddens. The defect here is a stale
argument in a file a reader will trust, not a hole in coverage.

THE WORK. Two PRs, the usual discipline. (1) An authorization in scripts/rail-renames.json carrying
the pairs that rewrite the comment lines to state what the assertion now reaches, and to name the
forwarding rail that carries the rest. (2) The edit. Each pair is one line of printable ASCII, 120
chars or fewer, expression-only -- the guard refuses a pair that adds a line.

CONSIDER WHILE THERE. The stronger repair is a bounded-duration fixture in this file: a bundle that
busy-waits ~200ms refuses at 1ms every time and renders at 500ms every time, which restores the
original argument rather than retiring it. It needs a new `const`, which one-line pairs cannot add.
If that is wanted, the pair set must rewrite an existing line into the const, or the rail moves to a
new unfrozen file and this one is retired.

RAILS: three consecutive green runs of the edited file, plus the rails-guard exemption proving base
plus the declared pairs is byte-identical to the branch.
title: render-sandbox's 1ms rail carries a comment that outlives its assertion
